title: Third Conditional: Practice — Quiz 81
content:
## Third Conditional: Practice

Practise talking about an unreal past situation and its imagined result.

### Lesson focus

1. If you ___ me, I would have attended the party. (invited / had invited)
2. I would ___ earlier if I had got an early bus. (come / have come)
3. If he ___ at home, he would have answered the phone. (were / had been)

### Understand the pattern

The third conditional describes a past condition that did not occur and an imagined past result. Use if + had + past participle, then would have + past participle. Both parts look back at an alternative past.

### Worked answers and explanation

1. had invited
2. have come
3. had been

In 2, would must be followed by have come to describe the unreal past result. Were in 3 would normally suggest an unreal present condition, so it does not fit the past-result context as clearly as had been.

### Try another

Complete: If we had left earlier, we ___ the train. (catch)

### Suggested answer

Would have caught. Caught is the past participle of catch; 'would have catch' is not the correct verb form.
